items.paraphrase: State the population or distribution the scientific claim is meant to generalize to.
Explain why that particular population or distribution was chosen.
Explain why machine learning is an appropriate tool for the study's question.
Share the training and evaluation data with a persistent link or identifier pinning the exact dataset.
Share training, evaluation and results code with a link or identifier fixing the exact code version.
Describe the hardware and software environment the computations ran on.
Provide a README explaining how to regenerate the reported results from the shared data and code.
Provide one script that regenerates every reported result end to end.
Document where training and evaluation data came from, when collected, and how ground-truth labels were produced.
Describe the sampling frame, i.e. the distribution or set the dataset was drawn from.
Argue concretely why this dataset suits the modeling task.
Define the target the model predicts and summarise it statistically, per class if the target is categorical.
Report the sample size and how often each outcome occurs.
Report the share of missing values, split by class for categorical outcomes.
Argue that the sampling frame represents the population targeted by the claim.
State whether any samples were excluded and give the reason.
Explain how impossible or corrupted samples were handled.
List every transformation from raw data to model input, such as missing-value handling and scaling, ideally diagrammed.
Describe every trained model in detail.
Justify the chosen model families.
Explain the evaluation procedure, e.g. how data were partitioned for training versus testing or how folds were formed.
Describe how the reported model or models were selected among candidates.
Give hyperparameter tuning details for the reported model or models.
Justify that the baselines used for comparison are appropriate.
Show that preprocessing and modeling used only training data, never test data.
Explain how dependencies or duplicates across train and test partitions were handled, e.g. grouping related samples together.
Argue why every input used by the model is legitimately available and cannot reveal the label.
Report every performance metric and justify the one used to pick the final model.
Report uncertainty estimates such as confidence intervals and explain how they were computed.
Justify any statistical tests used and check that their assumptions hold.
Provide evidence that the results hold beyond the study data (external validity).
State the settings in which the findings are not expected to hold.
